title: Composite Model/Route Timeline + Token Waterfall — Dashboard & Chart Specs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact dashboard panel that surfaces per-model and per-route performance across time with two coordinated visualizations: (1) a percentile timeline for latency + throughput overlays and (2) a token waterfall that shows token count distribution and token-type breakdown per request bucket. Goal: give engineers a single glance into latency regressions, throughput shifts, and token composition impact on cost and latency.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Timeline shows p50/p90/p99 latency lines with throughput as area behind, selectable time window (1h/6h/24h/7d). 2) Token waterfall aggregates recent requests into decile buckets and visualizes median token split (prompt/system/response) per bucket. 3) Hover tooltips expose request sample IDs, sample prompt length, cache hit/miss, model variant, route tag. 4) Threshold overlays configurable per-route. 5) Panel integrates into per-route and per-model views and respects project-level filter state.
chart_specs:
LATENCY TIMELINE:
- metrics: latency_p50, latency_p90, latency_p99 (ms)
- aggregation: time_bucketed percentiles computed on request-level end-to-end latency; window aggregation options: rolling 1m, 5m, 15m for high-res; display resolution adjusted by time range
- visualization: multi-line chart with shaded band between p50 and p90, p99 as dashed line
- y-axis: log scale option (toggle) with labeled tick presets (10ms, 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 500ms, 1s)
- x-axis: time; user-selectable range presets and custom range
- overlays: SLA threshold line (configurable per-route), incident annotation pins (clickable)

THROUGHPUT LAYER (COMBINED ON TIMELINE):
- metric: requests_per_second (RPS) as area underlay with distinct color and vertical scaling on secondary y-axis
- aggregation: per time bucket sum of requests; hover shows bucket-level distribution by status code

TOKEN WATERFALL CHART:
- purpose: show how token counts (and token types) correlate with latency and cost per request cohort
- x-axis: cohort buckets (deciles by latency or by request frequency depending on user choice)
- y-axis: token count (units) stacked by token type: system, prompt, user, response, metadata
- aggregation: cohort-level median and interquartile ranges; optional violin overlay for distribution shape
- interactions: click cohort to expand sample list (paged) with sample request IDs and links to full trace; color legend pinned to top
- annotations: estimated token cost per cohort calculated using active pricing profile

GENERAL METADATA FOR CHARTS:
- color palette: semantic palette with accessibility-checked contrast; latency lines use red/orange/teal palette; throughput area uses muted blue; token stacks use categorical palette with consistent mapping across all pages
- sampling: for high-traffic routes apply uniform sample rate with indication of sample fraction in chart header; for debug mode allow full-sample playback
- storage/compute considerations: percentile calculation should be pre-aggregated in metric pipeline (not client-side) and support adaptive downsampling for wide ranges
- telemetry: each chart interaction emits analytics event (zoom, cohort click, threshold toggle) for product telemetry
interactions:
- cross-filtering: cohort selection on token waterfall filters timeline to show only requests in that cohort.
- linked drilldown: timeline hover exposes 'Open samples' to show top 10 representative traces (links open console trace view).
- zoom & pan: brush-to-zoom on timeline; double-click resets to preset range.
- compare mode: allow toggling a second timeline to compare two model versions or two routes side-by-side.
- annotations: users can pin notes to time ranges (team-only or org-shared).
tradeoffs:
- Accuracy vs. cost: high-resolution percentile calculations are expensive; recommend pre-aggregated streaming percentiles with support for optional on-demand exact computation for small ranges.
- Viz density vs. clarity: combining throughput + latency helps story-telling but risks cognitive overload; mitigations: progressive disclosure (show p50 + p90 by default, p99 behind a toggle) and compact sparklines in route lists.
- Sampling vs. fidelity for token waterfall: to keep UI responsive, we sample requests for waterfall cohorts. Add explicit sample fraction display and allow 'full sample' for low-volume routes.
- Storage window: long-term storage of raw token breakdowns is costly; keep detailed token histograms for 90d and aggregated summaries for 365d.
review_feedback: 2025-03-11 - PM Jess Li: Prefer showing p95 instead of p99 on default view; p99 behind toggle. Concern about noise from p99 spikes.
2025-03-12 - Eng (infra) Miguel Santos: Confirm percentile computation is supported in the metrics pipeline. If not, we'll need a short infra spike; flagged as dependency ENG-40210.
2025-03-13 - Design review (internal) Claire Nguyen: Token color mapping needs stronger contrast and a legend anchor; recommend using patterned fills for small screens.
2025-03-14 - Privacy/Security (Samir Rao): Avoid including raw prompt text in hover/tooltips by default; show redacted prompt or 'view' link that requires elevated permission.
decisions: Default timeline will show p50 and p90 lines; p95 and p99 available via toggle per feedback.
Token waterfall will display cohort medians + IQR; violin overlay optional behind an 'advanced' toggle.
Prompt content will be redacted in tooltips; a 'view sample' action will link to audited trace view requiring RBAC permission.
